info.name: CronFetch API
info.description:
REST API for CronFetch — watch job-listing pages, record postings that match your experience band, preferred locations, and role, and push each new match to Telegram.

## Setup
1. Start the backend: `python app.py` (serves http://127.0.0.1:5000).
2. This collection has a `base_url` variable already set to that address — change it under the collection's **Variables** tab if you run elsewhere.
3. Run **Sites > Create site** first: its test script stores the new id in the `site_id` collection variable, which the other Sites requests reuse.
4. For Telegram: copy `.env.example` to `.env`, fill in `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`/`TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` (instructions in that file), restart the server, then run **Notify > Send test message** to confirm it works.

## Auto-detection
You only send `name` and `url`. On create, the API fetches the page and figures out the CSS selector for one job listing itself, returning the result under `detection` and storing it on the site. Pass `item_selector` explicitly only to override that. **Re-detect selector** re-runs it (e.g. after fixing a URL, or if a board changes its markup).

## Filters
`min_experience`/`max_experience`, `locations`, and `roles` are independent filters — a listing is only recorded when **all** pass. `min_experience`/`max_experience` describe a band: give only `min_experience` for a point match at that level (old behaviour), only `max_experience` for "nothing more senior than N years", or both for a real range; `min_experience` can't exceed `max_experience` (400 otherwise). `locations` and `roles` are each a list (e.g. `["India", "Remote"]`, `["Engineering", "Software Developer"]`); a listing matches a list filter when its card text contains **any one** entry, case-insensitively (OR within a filter, AND across filters). `null`/omitted on any field disables that filter.

## Notifications
Every `POST /api/run-now` (manual or the 15-min scheduler) ends by pushing each new match to Telegram as one message (title, experience/location/role, url) and marking it `sent` in `/api/history`. If Telegram isn't configured, or a send fails, the match stays `pending` and is retried on the next run (or via **Notify > Retry pending**) — nothing is lost.

## Typical flow
Create site → check `detection` in the response → Run now (first call seeds silently) → Run now again → List jobs / List history / check `notified` in the Run now response.

request.description:
Add a site to watch.

| field | required | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | display name |
| `url` | yes | listings page to fetch |
| `min_experience` | no | whole number of years. Alone, it's a point match (a listing is kept only when its own range contains this value — the original single-value behaviour). |
| `max_experience` | no | whole number of years. Alone, it means "nothing requiring more than this" (band `[0, max_experience]`). Given together with `min_experience`, the two form a real range and a listing is kept when its own range **overlaps** that band. `min_experience` > `max_experience` is rejected with 400. `null` / omitted on both = no experience filter. |
| `locations` | no | list of location strings to match against (frontend gives fixed choices, e.g. `["India", "Remote"]`), or a comma-separated string. A listing is kept when its card text contains any one of them (case-insensitive substring). `null` / omitted / `[]` = no filter. |
| `roles` | no | list of role/title keywords (e.g. `["Engineering", "Software Developer"]`), or a comma-separated string. Same substring-OR matching as `locations`. `null` / omitted / `[]` = no filter. |
| `item_selector` | no | **override** the auto-detected selector. One element per job card. |
| `css_selector` | no | fallback selector, used only when `item_selector` is empty and nothing was auto-detected |

All filters are independent — a listing needs to pass the experience band AND `locations` AND `roles` to be recorded.

The response includes a `detection` object when auto-detection ran:
```
"detection": {
  "ok": true,
  "selector": "li.section29__search-results-li",
  "count": 15,
  "sample": ["Senior IT Software Engineer ...", ...],
  "alternatives": ["..."],
  "note": "auto-detected (score 110, 15 listings)"
}
```
`ok: false` means the page is JavaScript-rendered or the URL failed — the site is still created; fix the URL and call **Re-detect selector**, or set `item_selector` yourself with **Update site**.

The test script saves the returned `id` into the `site_id` variable.

Re-run auto-detection for an existing site and save the result. Use after correcting a site's `url`, or when a board has changed its markup and checks started failing. Returns the site row with a `detection` object (same shape as on create). A successful run sets `item_selector` and `selector_source` to `auto`.

Edit any subset of `name`, `url`, `css_selector`, `item_selector`, `min_experience`, `max_experience`, `locations`, `roles`. Send `null` on any filter field to turn it off. The `min_experience` ≤ `max_experience` check runs against the **resulting** site (your payload merged over what's already stored), so patching just one bound is rejected if it conflicts with the other bound already saved. Setting `item_selector` here marks `selector_source` as `manual` (auto-detection won't overwrite it); setting it to `""`/`null` clears that. 404 if the id does not exist.
Remove a site. Its jobs are deleted too (cascade). 404 if the id does not exist.

Last 100 matched listings, newest first. Each row includes `site_name`, `url`, the parsed `experience_min` / `experience_max` (either may be null), `matched_location`, and `matched_role` — whichever entry from the site's `locations` / `roles` filters was found in this listing (null when that site has no such filter).

Last 200 log rows. `status` is one of: `pending` (a match found but not yet sent to Telegram, or Telegram isn't configured / the last send failed), `sent` (delivered to Telegram), `error` (a fetch/parse failure), `info` (e.g. first-run seeding notice). Rows for a job match carry `job_id`; others have it `null`.

Run the check immediately for every site instead of waiting for the 15-minute timer.

Response `result` summary:
- `new_jobs` — matched listings recorded this run (these create `pending` history rows, then get sent to Telegram before the response comes back)
- `skipped` — listings that failed the experience, location, or role filter (or had no detectable experience when a filter is set)
- `seeded` — listings recorded silently on a site's **first** check (no alerts)
- `errors` — sites that failed to fetch
- `details` — the same numbers broken down per site
- `notified` — `{sent, failed, skipped}` from the Telegram push: `skipped: true` means Telegram isn't configured (nothing was attempted); `failed` rows stay `pending` and are retried next time

The **first** Run now after creating a site only seeds; matches start alerting from the second run onward.
Returns `{"configured": true|false}` — whether `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` and `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` are both set in the environment. Doesn't verify they're actually valid — use **Send test message** for that.

Sends a one-off plain-text message to your configured chat, independent of any job data. Use this right after setting up `.env` to confirm the bot token and chat id actually work.

- `400` — not configured (env vars missing)
- `502` — configured but Telegram rejected the request (bad token, bot never messaged, wrong chat id, etc.) — `error` has Telegram's reason
- `200 {"ok": true}` — check your Telegram chat, the message should have arrived

Re-attempts delivery for every match still `pending` in `/api/history` (e.g. Telegram was down, or you've only just configured it after some matches piled up). Same `{sent, failed, skipped}` shape as the `notified` field on Run now. Safe to call anytime — already-`sent` rows aren't touched.
